record_id.reason: Licence Number is distinct across all 23169 rows, one row per current licence.

fields.reason: Licensee is the licence holder, which is the registered licensee name per the data. Some values are person names (rule 4); they are still mapped as legal_name and never inferred as sole_trader.
Trading As is the name the premises trades under, which is a trading name, not the registered name.
No explicit entity-type column exists, so entity_type_from_suffix on the Licensee name is the only permitted route. Individuals will resolve to unknown.
Premises street line. It is partial (no suburb or postcode in this field), so confidence is moderate. It is mapped to address.full because it is the only premises street address column.
Suburb of the premises; column name and values agree.
Premises postcode. Value 0 appears on 266 rows and will be rejected by the postcode transform, which is the intended behaviour.

unmapped.reason: Liquor licence class (e.g. Packaged Liquor Licence); no canonical field matches. It is not an entity type or industry code.
Trading hours or licence sub-type; no canonical field exists.
Patron capacity of the premises; no canonical field exists.
Local government area; no canonical field exists.
Liquor licensing region; no canonical field exists.
Metro or regional classification; no canonical field exists.
Geocode; no canonical field exists. Some coordinates do not match the stated suburb (for example Collingwood at -38.38), so they are unreliable in any case.
Geocode; no canonical field exists. See Latitude for quality concerns.
Licensee mailing address, not the premises address, so it is not mapped to address.*. There is no postal-address field in the ontology.
Licensee mailing suburb; no canonical postal field exists.
Licensee mailing postcode; no canonical postal field exists.

needs_transform.why: address.state is not in the file, but every row is a Victorian licence, so it would need a constant-value transform to set VIC. No such transform exists. Not mapping it is the conservative choice.

source_reliability_basis: Liquor Control Victoria is the statutory licensing regulator, so its register is high-trust for the fact that a licence is held by a named licensee (identity). The licensee name is the holder's declared name, and the trading name is self-declared. Address is the premises location from licence records, but there are quality issues: postcode 0 on 266 rows, and some coordinates do not match their suburb. Classification is weak because there is no entity-type column and the liquor licence category is not an entity type. Contact is weak because the only contact-like data is the licensee's postal address, which is not mapped.
